packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 17 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of work or author.
The fragment itself carries a modern pencil mark "VIII B 20/161" (image-006,
image-010), which I record as an observation only. I opened only PROMPT.md and
the image files of this packet. Beyond plain viewing I made enlarged, rotated
and contrast-stretched working copies of the tiles in a private scratch
directory, because the supplied tiles are small (c. 575-693 px wide) and the
ink is very pale. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used. (When saving
my responses, a directory listing of the responses folder showed me the file
names of other packets' responses; I did not open any of them.)

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 (overview, face 1, with ruler): a tall narrow vertical strip,
  c. 5 cm wide and c. 19-20 cm high by the ruler, left edge torn irregularly,
  right edge straight with a blank margin c. 0.7 cm. Upright text, one column
  (or one column of several: lines run from the torn left edge to the margin),
  c. 35 lines, very pale brown ink on greyed parchment. Near the top a
  horizontal fold with 2-3 lines of darker text above it. About one third down
  there is one line in a noticeably LARGER script (a heading or display line)
  with a red mark at its left end. A red initial or paraph c. two thirds down.
  Dark smudges/blots in the lower third and a horizontal crease. At the foot,
  separated by a blank band, six lines in a smaller, more cursive hand with at
  least three words underlined (a note or addition in the lower margin -
  tentative). Small dark marks at intervals in the right margin (possibly
  offset or line-end letters of an adjacent column; not legible).
- image-002 to image-005: four overlapping tiles of face 1, top to bottom.
- image-006 (overview, face 2): the reverse, strip now with straight edge at
  left and wide blank margin at left (c. 1 cm), torn at right. Upright pale text,
  c. 30 lines. A large red initial "E" (c. 4 lines high) with thin pen-flourish
  lines and small loops in ink, about half-way down; a red paraph/bracket-like
  mark a few lines below it. Dark smudges below that. At the top, crossing the
  manuscript text at 90 degrees, dark PRINTED black-letter text (offset or
  adhering paper from a printed book). Pencil shelfmark-like note at the foot.
- image-007 to image-010: four overlapping tiles of face 2, top to bottom.
- No running title seen. No interlinear gloss seen. The tiles do not have the
  resolution to settle letter forms; most of what follows is tentative.

SELECTED SPANS
1. Printed text on face 2 (image-007), because it is the only crisp text.
2. Face 1, display line and the c. 14 lines below it (image-003, top of -004).
3. Face 1, foot note in smaller hand (image-005).
4. Face 2, lines around the red initial (image-008, image-009).
Unread: face 1 top block (image-002), face 1 lower third under the blots
(image-004), almost all of face 2.

SPAN 1 - printed text, image-007, read with the image turned 90 degrees
(lines here are vertical in the supplied image; numbered from the inner side)
image-007(rot) P1: [upper line, mirror-faint] ...  (two further faint lines above, illegible)
image-007(rot) P2: K[...]i(?) : 2    (small heading-like line, mostly lost)
image-007(rot) P3: Bozjch Přik[á]zanj  [..]
image-007(rot) P4: [..]es mjti B[..]  gin.
image-007(rot) P5: [..] Kr[...]
image-007(rot) P6: Summa těch Přikáz[...]
Notes: black-letter type with j for long i and háček/acute marks; reads
left-to-right (not mirrored), so it is either adhering printed paper or a
double offset. It is unrelated to the manuscript text in layout. To the right
of it, fainter printed lines: "[..]ossobě(?) ..." / "[...] 300 0(?)..." - not
securely read.

SPAN 2 - face 1, image-003 (line numbers from the top of image-003; lines 1-3
of that tile repeat the last lines of image-002)
image-003 L1-L3: [overlap with image-002; pale, illegible apart from single letters "...sit a s...", "...p...u...m"]
image-003 L4 (larger script, red mark at left): [I/H]em(?)[......] as[...]ad(?)   - a display line; letters "em" then minims, then "a ſſ ... ad"; not read as words
image-003 L5: ad(?) p(ro)p(?)[....] pri(?)
image-003 L6: iij. h[.......]
image-003 L7: t(?)ra(?) thoma(?)[.] simili(?)t(er)(?)   [faint red stroke at the left edge]
image-003 L8: p(re)missis(?) uo(?) d(omi)n(u)m(?)
image-003 L9: n(?) patrino(?)[.] [word illegible]
image-003 L10: ad missa(m)(?) [hole] [..]s(?) ad(?)
image-003 L11: plena(m)(?) p(er)mit(?)[...]
image-003 L12: [paraph-like sign] iiij. s(?)e(?)xta(m)(?) [..]
image-003 L13: [.]lori(?) ad(?) sis(?) pleniter(?)
image-003 L14: [sign] xiiij(?). ai(?) s[...] i(n)[..]
image-003 L15: a p(re)d(i)c(t)us(?) de biles(?)
image-003 L16: [.] hildes(?) i[..] [..]re     (reddish stain over the right half)
image-003 L17: e unde i(?)[.] bu[..]re(?)
image-003 L18: dimid(?)[..] [illegible]
Notes: I can see roman numerals with points ("iij.", "iiij.", "xiiij."?) at or
near line beginnings and paraph-like signs before two of them; that is an
observation of shapes. Every word above is doubtful; the ink is pale and the
tile is too small to separate minims. I have not turned these into sense.
image-004 continues (overlap of L15-L18 at its top) with c. 14 more lines:
image-004 L5: [..] celebrare(?) [..]
image-004 L6: [..] p(?) una(?) [..] 
image-004 L9: [red initial or paraph] [...]
image-004 L13: [...] est   (line ends in "est" or "eſt")
all other lines there: [illegible] (blots, crease).

SPAN 3 - face 1 foot, smaller hand, image-005 (numbered from the first line of
the note; the two lines above the blank band are the end of the main text and
are illegible)
image-005 N1: [..]ny(?). Consule [underlined] eti(am)(?) non solu(m)(?)
image-005 N2: [..] o(?)[..]. Consule [underlined] [.]sec(?)[.....]
image-005 N3: [..] subueni(?)[...] [..] dx(?) eli[..]t(?) q(?)
image-005 N4: [..]ing(?). Rege [underlined, preceded by a paraph-like sign] [.....] colere(?)
image-005 N5: [..] ma(n)ib(us)(?) deligat(?) [..] fer[...]
image-005 N6: [..] [..] (et) infamia. Qui(?) [...]
Notes: "Consule" twice and "Rege"(?) are underlined, which looks like lemmata
followed by explanation (tentative: gloss or commentary on short imperatives).
The left end of each line is lost at the tear/turn-in.

SPAN 4 - face 2, image-008 / image-009 (image-009 repeats the initial and the
lines beside it)
image-008 L1-L10 (above the initial): c. 10 lines, pale; isolated shapes only:
  L4 "offer(?)[...]", L5 "[...] ad(?) ...", L6 "Sancti(?) [...]", L8 "[...] ab(?) de(?) ...";
  none securely read.
image-008 L11 / image-009 L1: [large red initial E, 4 lines high, pen-flourished] [.] dobo(?)[...]  / "ſi(?) Nobo[..]"  - first line beside the initial is in slightly larger letters; cut at the tear
image-009 L2: p(ro)uiden(?)[...]
image-009 L3: [..]
image-009 L4 (first full-width line under the initial): a s(?)um(?)[..] [..] ust(?)[..]
image-009 L5: resistat(?) [..]ito(?) [...]
image-009 L6: [..] [..]
image-009 L7: dam(?) [..] [....]
image-009 L8: [red paraph with a long horizontal stroke over the line] [illegible]
image-009 L9 onward: under dark blots, [illegible]; the last line before the
  blank foot (also top of image-010) begins "thuc(?). (et)(?) [...]".
image-010: blank lower margin with the pencil note "VIII B 20/161" (the last
  figure is on image-006; image-010 crops it after "1" plus a further digit).

LIMITATIONS
- This is the weakest of my packets: the tiles for this item are low
  resolution and the ink is extremely pale, on both faces. The gaps above
  reflect what the supplied pixels allow; I looked at every tile plain,
  enlarged and contrast-stretched.
- All lines are incomplete on the torn side; column structure beyond this
  strip is unknown.
- Whether the foot note on face 1 belongs to the main text is unknown.
- Suggested: native-resolution tiles (at least 3x the present pixel density),
  ideally UV or infrared, of image-003/-004 (face 1) and image-008/-009
  (face 2); and a crop of the right margin of face 1 to check the marginal marks.
